title: Real-world Japanese
intro: Exams measure what you know. These guides are about what actually happens in Japan: how people really talk, what staff say to you, the signs on every wall, and the numbers on every price tag. Read them any time; each takes a few minutes and has audio.

guides.title: How people really talk
guides.summary: Contractions, particles, fillers and the gap between textbook and street.

sections.title: Polite is safe, plain is normal
body: Textbooks teach です・ます first because it is never wrong. But friends, family, classmates and most people under forty talk to each other in plain form, and television, games and social media are almost entirely plain. If you only know polite forms you will understand half of what you hear.

The rule of thumb: polite with strangers, staff, superiors and anyone older; plain with friends, children and people who switch to plain with you first. When in doubt, stay polite and let the other person set the level.

items.jp: 食べました → 食べた
items.kana: たべました → たべた

items.jp: 学生です → 学生だ / 学生
items.kana: がくせいです → がくせいだ / がくせい
items.en: am a student (だ is often dropped in speech, especially by women)
Are you going? (rising intonation replaces か)

items.jp: いいですね → いいね
items.kana: いいですね → いいね

sections.title: Contractions you hear constantly
body: Spoken Japanese squeezes common endings. These six account for most of the difference between what you learned and what you hear.

items.kana: たべている → たべてる
items.en: is eating. The い disappears; also 〜でる (読んでる).

items.kana: わすれてしまった → わすれちゃった
items.en: I forgot (and it's too late). 〜でしまう → 〜じゃう (飲んじゃった).

items.kana: かっておく → かっとく
items.en: buy it in advance. 〜でおく → 〜どく.

items.kana: いかなければ → いかなきゃ
items.en: have to go. Often the ending ならない is dropped entirely.

items.kana: たべてはだめ → たべちゃだめ
たなかというひと → たなかってひと
items.romaji: tanaka to iu hito → tanaka tte hito
items.en: a person called Tanaka. って also quotes: 来るって (they said they'll come) and marks a topic: これって何？

items.kana: いくのです → いくんです / いくんだ
items.romaji: iku no desu → iku n desu / iku n da
items.en: the explaining ん. Questions: 行くの？ (casual), 行くんですか (polite).

items.kana: わからない → わからん
items.en: don't know (Kansai and western dialects; you will hear it).

sections.title: Sentence-final particles
body: The little sounds at the end of a sentence carry attitude. Overuse よ and you sound pushy; never use ね and you sound cold.

items.en: Cold, isn't it. Seeks agreement; the friendliest particle.
It's good, you know. Gives information the listener lacks; can sound insistent.
Tomorrow's a day off, right? Checking something you think is true.
Maybe I'll go… Wondering aloud; softens a decision.
See, you can do it! Casual じゃない; very Tokyo.
What time was it again? Trying to recall.
Nice… (to oneself, envious or admiring). Rough command when attached to a verb: 行くな = don't go.
So, yesterday, … A pause filler inside sentences (Tokyo casual).
Let's go! (ぞ・ぜ: rough, male, anime-flavoured; わ: soft, mostly older women or Kansai). Recognise them; rarely use them.

sections.title: Fillers and reactions
body: Silence in a conversation is uncomfortable in Japanese. Fillers buy time; reactions (aizuchi) show you are listening. Native speakers produce one every few seconds and expect you to as well.

items.en: like… / kind of (the most common filler among young people)

items.jp: うん / ええ / はい
items.en: mm-hm / yes (casual → polite); said while the other person talks, not only to answer
what? no way (surprise or mild complaint, depending on tone)
wow / uh-oh / amazing / awful. Means whatever the tone says. Young, casual.
hey / bye / nice work (casual お疲れさま; among friends and colleagues it is simply a greeting)

sections.title: Saying no without saying no
body: A flat いいえ is rare. Refusals are hedged, left unfinished, or wrapped in regret. Learn to hear them, and to produce them, or you will seem blunt.

items.en: It's a bit… (= no). The trailing-off is the answer.
I'll think about it (= probably no).
I'm fine / no thanks (to an offer). Also 'it's okay' as reassurance; tone decides.
It's kind of you, but… (regretful refusal)

guides.title: What staff say to you
guides.summary: Service keigo decoded: the questions at every counter and what to answer.

sections.title: The pattern
body: Shop and restaurant staff use the most formal register you will hear, fast and in a sing-song voice. The good news: it is a script. The same thirty sentences appear in every shop in the country, and your side of the conversation is はい, いいえ, お願いします and 大丈夫です.

Verbs are dressed up: 〜ます becomes 〜いたします or お〜します when staff do it, and ご〜 / お〜 plus になります・ください when you do it. Ignore the decoration and listen for the key noun: 袋 (bag), お支払い (payment), 温め (heating), ご注文 (order).

items.note: No reply needed; a nod is plenty.

items.jp: ポイントカードはお持ちですか
items.kana: ポイントカードはおもちですか
items.romaji: pointo kaado wa omochi desu ka
items.en: Do you have a point card?
items.note: ないです / 持っていません.

items.jp: 袋はご利用ですか / 袋にお入れしますか
items.kana: ふくろはごりようですか
items.note: お願いします or 大丈夫です. Bags cost a few yen.
お願いします / そのままで.

items.jp: お箸はお付けしますか
items.kana: おはしはおつけしますか
items.note: はい、お願いします.

items.jp: お支払いはどうなさいますか
items.kana: おしはらいはどうなさいますか
items.note: カードで / 現金で / 〇〇ペイで.

items.jp: 一括でよろしいですか
items.kana: いっかつでよろしいですか
items.note: はい. Instalments are a Japanese-card feature; foreign cards are always single.

items.kana: えんおあずかりします
items.note: Then 〇〇円のお返しです: your change.

items.jp: レシートはご利用ですか
items.kana: レシートはごりようですか
items.note: はい / いらないです.

items.jp: ありがとうございました。またお越しくださいませ
items.kana: ありがとうございました。またおこしくださいませ
items.note: どうも or nothing.
一人 / 二人 / 三人です, or hold up fingers.

items.jp: ご予約はされていますか
items.kana: ごよやくはされていますか
items.note: はい、〇〇で予約しています / していません.

items.jp: 禁煙席と喫煙席、どちらになさいますか
items.kana: きんえんせきときつえんせき、どちらになさいますか
items.romaji: kin'enseki to kitsuenseki, dochira ni nasaimasu ka
items.note: 禁煙で.

items.jp: お決まりになりましたらお呼びください
items.kana: おきまりになりましたらおよびください
items.en: Call me when you have decided.
items.note: Press the button or say すみません.

items.jp: ご注文はお決まりですか
items.kana: ごちゅうもんはおきまりですか
items.note: はい / もう少し待ってください.

items.jp: 以上でよろしいでしょうか
items.kana: いじょうでよろしいでしょうか
items.note: はい、以上です.

items.jp: お飲み物はいかがですか
items.kana: おのみものはいかがですか
items.note: お水で大丈夫です.

items.jp: こちらでお召し上がりですか、お持ち帰りですか
items.kana: こちらでおめしあがりですか、おもちかえりですか
items.romaji: kochira de omeshiagari desu ka, omochikaeri desu ka
items.note: ここで / 持ち帰りで.

items.jp: お会計はご一緒でよろしいですか
items.kana: おかいけいはごいっしょでよろしいですか
items.romaji: okaikei wa goissho de yoroshii desu ka
items.note: はい / 別々でお願いします (separately).

items.jp: お手洗いは奥の左手です
items.kana: おてあらいはおくのひだりてです
items.romaji: otearai wa oku no hidarite desu
items.en: The toilet is at the back on the left.
items.note: Ask with お手洗いはどこですか.

items.kana: しょうしょうおまちください

items.jp: お待たせいたしました
items.kana: おまたせいたしました
items.en: Sorry to have kept you waiting.
items.note: Said even after ten seconds.

items.jp: こちらにご記入ください
items.kana: こちらにごきにゅうください

items.jp: 身分証明書をお願いします
items.kana: みぶんしょうめいしょをおねがいします
items.note: Passport or residence card.

items.kana: もうしわけございません

items.jp: ご利用いただけません
items.kana: ごりよういただけません
items.en: You cannot use (this). (= not available / not accepted)

items.kana: ただいままんせきです
items.note: どのくらい待ちますか: how long is the wait?

items.kana: ほんじつはへいてんしました

guides.title: Numbers in the wild
guides.summary: Prices, times, dates and counters as they are actually said.

sections.title: Prices
body: Prices are said in full, fast. The sound changes are the trap: 300 is さんびゃく, 600 is ろっぴゃく, 800 is はっぴゃく; 3,000 is さんぜん, 8,000 is はっせん. 10,000 is いちまん, so 25,000 is にまんごせん. Listen for the まん.

items.kana: さんびゃくはちじゅうえん
せんきゅうひゃくはちじゅうえん
ろくせんろっぴゃくえん
いちまんさんぜんごひゃくえん
ぜいこみ / ぜいべつ
items.en: tax included / tax extra (10%, 8% on food)

sections.title: Time
body: Hours use 時, minutes 分; four, seven and nine o'clock are よじ, しちじ, くじ, never よん・なな・きゅう. Minutes change sound: 1分 いっぷん, 3分 さんぷん, 6分 ろっぷん, 8分 はっぷん, 10分 じゅっぷん. Timetables use the 24-hour clock; speech uses ごぜん / ごご or あさ / よる.

items.kana: じゅうはちじさんじゅっぷんはつ
なんじかん / なんぷん
さんじゅっぷんくらい

sections.title: Dates
body: Days 1–10 and a few others are irregular: ついたち, ふつか, みっか, よっか, いつか, むいか, なのか, ようか, ここのか, とおか, じゅうよっか (14), はつか (20), にじゅうよっか (24). Everything else is number + にち. Years can be Western (2026年) or era-based (令和8年, Reiwa 8) on official forms.

items.en: 1 April (4月 is しがつ, not よんがつ)

items.kana: じゅうにがつにじゅうよっか
げつようび … にちようび
items.en: Monday to Sunday: 月 火 水 木 金 土 日
public holiday (shops open, banks and offices shut)

sections.title: Counters you cannot avoid
body: You can get far with the generic ひとつ・ふたつ・みっつ for things, and 人 for people. These few others come up every day.

items.jp: 一人 / 二人 / 三人
items.kana: ひとり / ふたり / さんにん

items.jp: 一本 / 二本 / 三本
items.kana: いっぽん / にほん / さんぼん
items.en: long things: bottles, umbrellas, trains (本数)
cups and glasses (なまビール一杯)
nights (hotels): 二泊三日 two nights three days

items.jp: 一階 / 二階 / 三階
items.kana: いっかい / にかい / さんがい
items.en: floors: 地下一階 is basement 1

items.kana: いっぴき / いっとう / いちわ
items.en: small animals / large animals / birds (and rabbits)

guides.title: Politeness in practice
guides.summary: Plain, polite and respectful: the same sentence at three levels, and when each is right.

sections.title: Three levels, one language
body: Every Japanese sentence is pitched at a level: plain (friends), polite です・ます (default with strangers), and keigo (respectful 尊敬語 for what others do, humble 謙譲語 for what you do; used with customers, bosses and in formal settings). You produce keigo rarely until you work in Japan, but you hear it constantly, so learn to recognise the forms.
The safest path: speak polite, understand keigo, use plain only when the other person does.

items.jp: 食べる → 食べます → 召し上がる / いただく
items.kana: たべる → たべます → めしあがる / いただく
items.en: eat: plain → polite → respectful (they eat) / humble (I eat)

items.jp: 行く → 行きます → いらっしゃる / 参る
items.kana: いく → いきます → いらっしゃる / まいる
items.en: go (いらっしゃる also covers come and be)

items.jp: 見る → 見ます → ご覧になる / 拝見する
items.kana: みる → みます → ごらんになる / はいけんする
items.romaji: miru → mimasu → goran ni naru / haiken suru

items.jp: 言う → 言います → おっしゃる / 申す
items.kana: いう → いいます → おっしゃる / もうす
items.en: say (田中と申します: my name is Tanaka)

items.jp: する → します → なさる / いたす
items.kana: する → します → なさる / いたす
items.en: do (どうなさいますか: what would you like to do?)

items.jp: いる → います → いらっしゃる / おる
items.kana: いる → います → いらっしゃる / おる
items.en: be (田中はおりません: Tanaka is not here, said of your own colleague)

items.jp: 知っている → 知っています → ご存じだ / 存じている
items.kana: しっている → しっています → ごぞんじだ / ぞんじている
items.romaji: shitte iru → shitte imasu → gozonji da / zonjite iru

items.jp: もらう → もらいます → — / いただく
items.kana: もらう → もらいます → いただく
items.en: receive (〜ていただけますか: could you … for me?)

sections.title: Mistakes that mark a learner
body: Using あなた for 'you': use the person's name + さん instead; あなた sounds distant or scolding. Saying さようなら to people you will see tomorrow: use お疲れさまです, 失礼します or また明日. Answering はい to いらっしゃいませ: it is not a question. Using 〜たい about other people's wishes: say 〜たがっている or 〜たいそうです. Saying ごめんなさい to a shop assistant: すみません is the adult apology; ごめん is for friends.

guides.title: Reading and listening in the wild
guides.summary: Free sources of real Japanese, ordered by level, and how to use them.

sections.title: Why you still need this
body: This app gives you the characters, the words and the grammar; reading anything you meet in Japan comes from mileage with real texts. Plan on reading something real every day from the N4 stage onwards, looking up only what blocks understanding. Comprehension at 80% is the sweet spot: hard enough to learn, easy enough to keep going.
The sources below are free or have a free tier, are made for learners or are real content with help attached, and contain nothing that needs an account to start.

links.name: NHK News Web Easy
links.note: Daily news rewritten in simple Japanese with furigana, audio and a dictionary on tap. The single best next step after N5.

links.name: Tadoku free graded readers
links.note: Hundreds of short illustrated books by level, free to read online. Read many easy ones rather than one hard one.

links.name: Satori Reader
links.note: Serialised stories with per-sentence explanations and audio; several series are free.

links.name: Yomitan (browser dictionary)
links.note: Hover over any Japanese word in your browser for readings and meanings. Turns the whole web into graded reading.

links.name: NHK News (regular) and Aozora Bunko
links.note: Real news, and the free library of out-of-copyright Japanese literature. Aim for short modern pieces first.

links.name: Japanese subtitles on streaming services
links.note: Watch Japanese shows with Japanese subtitles, not English. Pause and shadow a line now and then; it is the closest thing to living there.

sections.title: Talking to people
body: Speaking well comes from speaking. Language-exchange apps (HelloTalk, Tandem) pair you with Japanese speakers learning English; thirty minutes of messaging a day teaches the casual register faster than any textbook. Italki and similar sites offer tutors for a few hundred yen a lesson. In Japan itself, local international associations (国際交流協会) run free or near-free conversation groups in most cities.
Use the role-plays in Speak before each real situation: run the convenience store once in the app and the real one is easy.
